closed.content: Project atlas is deployed by running bin/ship.sh from the repository root.
Deploys to atlas staging are never automatic: someone runs bin/ship.sh --staging by hand.
The atlas test suite is run with cargo nextest run, not cargo test.
The branch under review is spike/consolidate.
The flaky test being chased this week is pagination_ordering in atlas-api.
To ship atlas you run the bin/ship.sh script at the top of the repo.
Deploying atlas means executing bin/ship.sh; the old make deploy target is gone.

answer:
All cleanup done. Here's what changed in the `atlas` memory space:

**Duplicates merged/closed:**
- Two near-identical "tests run via `cargo nextest run`, not `cargo test`" claims → kept one, closed the other.
- Three near-identical "deploy = `bin/ship.sh`" claims → merged into one: *"Project atlas is deployed by running bin/ship.sh from the repository root; the old make deploy target has been removed."*

**Real contradiction resolved:**
- Found (not flagged by the automated scan) two claims that directly conflicted: *"Merging to main deploys atlas to staging automatically"* vs. *"Deploys to atlas staging are never automatic: someone runs bin/ship.sh --staging by hand."* The "automatic" version had stronger reinforcement (accessed more recently, higher strength) — reads like staging deploys used to be manual and were later automated via CI-on-merge. Closed the outdated manual-deploy claim.

**Stale scaffolding removed:**
- *"The branch under review is spike/consolidate"* and *"The flaky test being chased this week is pagination_ordering in atlas-api"* — both filed as short-lived, both idle 40 days past their intended lifespan, neither durable. Closed rather than left to expire.

**Left alone:** the automated scan's `near_duplicates` and most of its `contradictions` were false positives — claims that only clustered because they're short and topically similar (e.g., container/registry/licensing facts), not because they say the same thing or disagree. I read each pair and didn't touch those.

One thing I didn't resolve: two claims both call something "feature flags in atlas" — one about Cargo build features (additive-only, gates `cargo check --all-features`), one about a runtime env-var toggle map. They could be two genuinely different systems sharing a name, or one could be stale. I left both since I can't tell from the store alone — worth a sanity check if it comes up.

Everything closed (not purged), so it's recoverable if any of this was wrong.
